title: Punctual purity of a rank-one Weil character on a curve
statement:
In the situation of
[thm-wf-rank-one-finite-geometric-image-curve], with $c$ and
$\varepsilon$ from [cor-wf-rank-one-degree-factorization-curve]
(applicable because $\chi(\Pi)$ is finite by that theorem), fix an embedding
$\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\hookrightarrow\mathbf C$, and use its
restriction to $E$ (equivalently, choose an embedding $E\hookrightarrow \mathbf C$ and an extension to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$). The rank-one lisse Weil sheaf
associated with $\chi$ by the
fundamental representation
is punctually $\iota$-pure of the
real weight

$$
w_\iota(\chi)=2\log_q|\iota(c)|,
$$

where $c=\chi(s)$ for any
degree-one element $s$.
The sheaf, degree, and punctual-purity conventions are those of
[def-wf-fundamental-representation], [def-wf-weil-group], [def-weil-punctual-weights].

Explicitly, for this embedding $\iota$, punctual purity means that for every closed point $x$ and every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of its local geometric-Frobenius operator $F_x$ [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], one has $|\iota(\alpha)|=\#\kappa(x)^{w_\iota(\chi)/2}$. This is the absolute-value condition of [def-weil-punctual-weights], applied also when $\iota$ is an embedding rather than a surjective isomorphism.

proof.text: The hypotheses on $U_0$ are precisely those of [lem-wf-curve-normal-smooth-compactification]. Its first conclusion says that $U_0$ is smooth over $\mathbf F_q$. Together with the given geometric connectedness, separatedness, finite type and pure dimension one, this puts $U_0$ in the curve setting of the sheaf–representation equivalence and local Frobenius comparison used below. Only smoothness is used; no compactification is chosen.

source.place: First paragraph, curve hypotheses for p-real-operations

proof.text: Apply [thm-wf-rank-one-finite-geometric-image-curve] to the given continuous $E^\times$-valued character: its hypotheses are unchanged, so $\chi(\Pi)$ is finite. Thus [cor-wf-rank-one-degree-factorization-curve] applies with the chosen degree-one $s$. It gives $c=\chi(s)\in E^\times$ and a finite-order character $\varepsilon$, with $\chi(w)=\varepsilon(w)c^{\deg(w)}$ for all $w$. Regard $\chi$ as the one-dimensional $\Qlb$-representation obtained from its $E$-line by scalar extension. By [prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence] it has a corresponding lisse Weil sheaf $L$; its geometric generic stalk, with the fundamental action of [def-wf-fundamental-representation], is this line. This is the rank-one associated sheaf of the statement.

source.place: First paragraph, factorization and the associated fundamental representation

proof.text: Fix a closed point $x$ of $U_0$ and put $d=[\kappa(x):\mathbf F_q]$. The closed-point clause of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] gives $d\ge1$ and the local operator $F_x$ on the stalk of $L$. By [p-real-operations], a geometric Frobenius representative at $x$ has degree $d$ and its characteristic factor on this stalk equals $\det(1-T\chi(F_x))$. As this is a one-dimensional representation, the factor is $1-T\chi(F_x)$; hence its sole eigenvalue is $\alpha_x=\chi(F_x)$. Conjugation does not change a character value, since $\chi(hF_xh^{-1})=\chi(h)\chi(F_x)\chi(h)^{-1}=\chi(F_x)$. The factorization in [cor-wf-rank-one-degree-factorization-curve] therefore gives $\alpha_x=\varepsilon(F_x)c^d$.

source.place: First paragraph and displayed eigenvalue factorization

proof.text: By [cor-wf-rank-one-degree-factorization-curve], $\varepsilon$ is a finite-order character, so choose $N\ge1$ with $\varepsilon(w)^N=1$ for all $w$. For every $w$, the field embedding preserves this identity, and complex multiplicativity gives $|\iota(\varepsilon(w))|^N=1$. This nonnegative real number $|\iota(\varepsilon(w))|$ must be $1$: a value below $1$ has $N$th power below $1$, and a value above $1$ has $N$th power above $1$. In particular, the eigenvalue from step 3 satisfies $|\iota(\alpha_x)|=|\iota(c)|^d$. This argument needs no surjectivity of $\iota$.

source.place: Second paragraph, root-of-unity modulus; elementary argument for embeddings

proof.text:
Put $a=|\iota(c)|>0$ (since $c\in E^\times$) and $w=2\log(a)/\log(q)$. Since $q$ is a finite-field cardinality, $q>1$. A basis of the degree-$d$ extension $\kappa(x)/\mathbf F_q$ identifies its elements with $d$-tuples over $\mathbf F_q$, so $\#\kappa(x)=q^d$. By the definition of real powers of positive numbers,
$$
(q^d)^{w/2}=\exp\bigl(d\log(q)\,\log(a)/\log(q)\bigr)=\exp(d\log(a))=a^d=|\iota(\alpha_x)|.
$$
This is the punctual-purity condition in [def-weil-punctual-weights] for the rank-one sheaf $L$, at every closed point. We use its displayed absolute-value formula, which is meaningful for the fixed embedding as well as for the isomorphisms allowed by that definition. Every $\alpha_x$ lies in $E$, so only $\iota|_E$ enters the condition.

source.place: Second displayed modulus identity and third paragraph, definition of purity

proof.text: Finally let $s'$ be any other degree-one element. Using the same factorization [cor-wf-rank-one-degree-factorization-curve] gives $\chi(s')=\varepsilon(s')c$. Step 4 applied to $w=s'$ yields $|\iota(\chi(s'))|=|\iota(c)|$. Consequently $2\log_q|\iota(\chi(s'))|=2\log_q|\iota(c)|$. Thus the displayed real weight is independent of the degree-one lift, as asserted.

source.place: Third paragraph, independence of the degree-one lift

proof_origin.place: Proof, three paragraphs; expanded curve hypotheses, elementary modulus and logarithm calculations

split_report.summary: Completed the existing blueprint route without creating nodes. Reused normal-curve smoothness, finite geometric image, the finite-order factorization, the sheaf–representation equivalence and the local Frobenius polynomial comparison. Expanded the root-of-unity and real logarithm calculations as elementary steps, explicitly valid for a field embedding. Clarified the imported embedding/isomorphism convention mismatch by spelling out the punctual-purity formula; all original hypotheses and conclusions remain. Read the tagged Lean candidates: they prove representation-level weights and lift independence, not the associated sheaf-level predicate of this item.
split_report.blueprint: Step 1 supplies the curve hypothesis for the first paragraph; steps 2–3 realize the first paragraph and its factorization. Steps 4–5 realize the second paragraph and purity conclusion. Step 6 realizes independence of the lift in the third paragraph. This is the purity portion of the fourth step of sk-p-real-rankone; the geometric finiteness portion remains thm-wf-rank-one-finite-geometric-image-curve.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q137-d5c45fa97 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all of the mathematics. Delivery: one commit holding the item and its report, no new nodes, no unit record changed; the item is not the unit's key node, so leaving realized empty is right. Statement: the hypotheses and conclusion are verbatim from the blueprint (master order 2628 and main-20261015 order 2972 have the same text). The worker added one paragraph that spells out the absolute-value condition for an embedding iota, where def-weil-punctual-weights is written for an isomorphism. Every eigenvalue lies in E, and every embedding of E into C extends to an isomorphism of Qlbar onto C, so the paragraph is equivalent to the definition and weakens nothing; d-real-setup itself fixes iota as an embedding. Route: every cited statement is on the route (own unit, sk-p-rankone, sk-i-real-compactification, sk-i-real-sheaves, sk-p-real-operations; the rest are definitions), no tool uses, no cycle, no SGA. Step 1: lem-wf-curve-normal-smooth-compactification has exactly the item's hypotheses, and its first conclusion gives the smoothness that the chapter's definition of a curve requires. Step 2: the finite-image theorem, then the factorization corollary (c=chi(s), finite-order epsilon, chi(w)=epsilon(w)c^deg w), then the sheaf from prop-wf-weil-sheaf-representation-equivalence, all taken from statements. Step 3: p-real-operations gives the degree-e_x geometric Frobenius class and P_x=det(1-T rho(F_x)); the degree sign agrees with def-wf-weil-group, so alpha_x=epsilon(F_x)c^d. That the stalk is one-dimensional is left implicit; it follows because F_x is invertible, so this is not a gap. Step 4: a direct root-of-unity modulus argument valid for any embedding, correctly used instead of lem-tw-root-of-unity-modulus, which needs an isomorphism. Step 5: #kappa(x)=q^d and the log/exp identity, with q>1 and |iota(c)|>0. Step 6: lift independence via the factorization applied to s'. proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses. Small cases tested: trivial and finite-order chi give weight 0; c=q^-1 gives weight -2, confirming the geometric-Frobenius sign; degree d>1; no rational point; change of lift. Duplicates: cor-mg-rankone-weight-from-element (sk-p-readout, off route) is an iff criterion for a supplied weight, not the same statement, and the item is an imported blueprint node. The slopmaster2 theorem IsLisse.isPunctuallyPure_of_finrank_eq_one (Purity.lean:162) is a representation-level predicate, so there is no exact attachment and lean_audit none is right. Mathlib searches: all three kinds recorded. No changes made.
